“Western Alliance’s third quarter results featured enhanced profitability, lower deposit costs, improved asset quality and stronger reserve coverage, as well as accelerated share repurchase activity,” said Kenneth A. Vecchione, Chairman, President and Chief Executive Officer. “Strong execution generated pre-provision net revenue 1 of $419 million, up $25 million, or 6.4%, year-over-year and earnings per share of $2.45, up $0.17, or 7.5%. Return on average assets of 1.12% and return on average tangible common equity 1 of 15.5% both increased for the second consecutive quarter. Deposit optimization actions totaling $4.5 billion over the past two quarters drove a $14 million, or 8%, quarterly decline in ECR-related deposit costs. Strong commercial banking deposit growth offset the optimization activity, keeping total deposits stable at $81.8 billion. Net interest income increased $11 million from the prior quarter, while net interest margin expanded 4 basis points quarterly to 3.57%. Asset quality improved notably, with nonaccrual loans declining $77 million, or approximately 14%, to 0.79% of funded HFI loans. Continued reserve building increased ACL coverage of funded HFI loans by 4 basis points to 0.93% and raised ACL coverage of nonaccrual loans from 96% to 118%. Net charge-offs declined 7 basis points quarterly to 0.30%, the midpoint of our 2026 guidance range. We continued to prioritize shareholder returns, repurchasing $92 million of shares.”
